subject: Sync: SDK changes for streaming + function-calls (summary & next steps)
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena@rivermark.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Sync: SDK changes for streaming + function-calls (summary & next steps)

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick write-up from our call so we have alignment on scope and next steps. I tried to keep this short and actionable.

Key pain you described
- High tail latency on short queries (sub-100 token responses) when you hit burst traffic from triage flows.
- Need deterministic throughput for reranking pipelines (embedding + top-k rerank) — cost sensitivity around token time and GPU utilization.
- Requirement to return structured patient-safety outputs (JSON schema) and call external diagnosis enrichment functions in a single request.

Goals you want to achieve in POC
- Streaming generation for triage UI (<200ms first-byte goal)
- Server-side rerank of up to 50 candidates with embedding scoring and a fallback cheap model
- Single API call that streams tokens while emitting structured JSON and invoking a function to fetch diagnosis codes.

What we propose (high level)
1) SDK changes: a new streaming+funcall helper in the JavaScript SDK that exposes a single handle for: initial prompt -> token stream -> function call event -> final structured output. Ben will ship a RFC and a reference example.
2) Performance knobs: recommended batching policy for your traffic pattern (max batch latency 12ms, dynamic burst slots) + KV-prefix caching for repeated symptom prefixes.
3) Rerank pattern: embeddings precompute (512-d) stored in your DB, Redwood will serve dense scoring in the pipeline with a cheap L2 fallback when GPU is saturated.

Open technical questions we flagged on the call
- Would you be able to share a small anonymized sample of triage prompts (5–10) and a sample set of 200 candidate responses for a rerank test? (we can sign an NDA if needed)
- Do you require HSM-backed keys for function payloads (for compliance)?
- Any hard SLA on first-byte time vs average completion time? We suggested prioritizing first-byte for the UI flow.

Immediate next steps and owners
- Mateo: send this summary + initial RFC link (today) — DONE (this email).
- Ben: produce a reference branch in the JS SDK demonstrating streaming with a function-call hook and an example that emits schema-validated JSON (ETA: 3 business days).
- Lena: share anonymized sample payloads and confirm whether procurement needs a separate POC SOW (ETA: EOD Thu).

Attachments attached: redwood-sdk-change-summary.pdf (design notes), rivermark-sample-payloads.json (redacted example).

If any of this looks off, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise Ben and I will start the branch and aim to have a runnable example by next Wednesday.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

1) We can share anonymized prompts and candidate responses — I’ll send a redacted .json by EOD Thursday. Will that be enough for your benchmarking?
2) We do require HSM-backed keys for anything that touches patient identifiers — for the POC we can remove identifiers, but long-term this is a hard requirement.
3) On SLAs: we don’t need strict contractual SLAs for the POC, but our product team prefers the first-byte under 250ms for the triage UI.

Hi Lena — looping in a quick technical note and the proposed checklist for the reference branch.

What I’ll ship in the PR (target Wed EOD):
- A new client helper: streamingFuncCall(streamOptions) that returns an async iterator of {type: 'token'|'func_call'|'done', data}. The func_call event includes a small metadata block for the external call.
- Example server-side handler that validates the final JSON against your provided schema and demonstrates a safe function invocation flow with an HSM option stub.
- A small perf harness that will replay your sample prompts (if provided) and produce a latency histogram (p50/p95/p99) and GPU utilization trace for a 2-A100 deployment.

Checklist for Rivermark for a smooth POC
- Provide redacted sample payloads (5–10 prompts + 200 candidates for rerank).
- Share the desired JSON schema for structured output (we’ll validate with Ajv in the example).
- Confirm whether you'd like the reference example to include on-prem (Private) instructions — if yes, provide a rough network topology.

If you’re okay I’ll open the PR and tag you both. Mateo, I’ll include the PDF summary as well.
